stage_state.summary_md:
### Communicating Across Levels

Designing with data aims to reduce reliance on "gut" decision making, which can break hierarchical structures. Data literacy invites discussion, challenge, and the potential to be wrong, diminishing top-down, hunch-based decisions. Data should be collected via multiple techniques (A/B testing, ethnographic field research, field deployments, surveys, lab studies, usability research), not just A/B testing. A 2007 paper by Ron Kohavi, Randal Henne, and Dan Sommerfield, "Practical Guide to Controlled Experiments on the Web: Listen to Your Customers not to the HIPPO," addressed this. Data resolves conflicts without relying on rank, hierarchy, or company politics.

John Ciancutti, former VP of Product Engineering at Netflix, described how data literacy across roles became a source of freedom and innovation. Patty McCord, former Chief Talent Officer at Netflix (12+ years), noted that having a mechanism to measure whether you are doing right by customers gives more people a voice in product development. Netflix's data-driven approach was universally accepted, starting from CEO Reed Hastings and CPO Neil Hunt driving it, but embraced by all levels from management to individual contributors.

At Netflix, even executives submit ideas to A/B testing. Reed Hastings would put his ideas into "his test cell" alongside other team proposals; if his cell didn't win, it wasn't launched. On rare occasions he might dictate exact implementation, but only on his test cell, which competed against others. This reinforced subjecting ideas to experimentation and accepting "failure" as a positive outcome, central to the company's view of how it should work. Shifting to a data-aware framework requires examining past decision-making patterns. If decisions were concentrated in few individuals, those people must recognize the value of user data, as their individual opinion's weight will diminish. This is a good point to check with yourself — are you comfortable seeing how incorporating data will change the weight of your own opinion?
